messages.author: 4c8abebaa7e886e1
messages.subject: vb.correction aborted warning
parts:
Hi,

I'm running across a new error about limit of vb.corrections being aborted (I have played around with the limit a bit) and was wondering how to interpret it.

I'm running a spatio-temporal model with interactions -- this is for teaching purposes and not because I necessarily believe in this model. I've left all the default priors etc. 

The code for the 4 models I'm running is below I've attached most of the output of verbose for one of the models (it wouldn't all fit in the Rstudio output window)  the warning that is generated by the type 2 and 3 but NOT type 1 and 4 models is below.  

I'm guessing the vb.correction is related to this paper https://arxiv.org/pdf/2111.12945.pdf and was wondering whether anyone had any idea what is going on and what sensible priors there might be -- if there are any in this situation.

Finally, prior to the latest update in r-inla (and R) the same code was running with a different warning (which I cannot quite remember right now)

This is by no means urgent but I'd be interested in any insights.

Thanks,
Sara

vac.mnth.typeI <- month_doses ~
  #structured spatial
  f(num_id, model="bym", graph=london.adj)+
  #structured time
  f(month, model="rw2") +
  #iid time
  f(month1, model="iid") +
  #interaction
  f(num_id.month, model="iid")

vac.mnth.typeI.inla <- inla(vac.mnth.typeI , family="poisson",
                      data = vac.mnth, offset=log(population),
                      control.predictor =list(compute=TRUE),
                      control.compute = list(dic=TRUE))

#check that there are the right amount of interaction terms
#this should be the number of boroughs (33)
#times the number of months (6)
length(vac.mnth.typeI.inla$marginals.random$num_id.month)


## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#temporal
month.int <- vac.mnth$month
#spatial
num_id.int <- vac.mnth$num_id


## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
vac.mnth.typeII <- month_doses ~
  f(num_id, model="bym", graph=london.adj) +
  f(month, model="rw2") +
  f(month1, model="iid") +
  f(num_id.int, model="iid",
    #iid on the spatial component
    group = month.int,
    control.group = list(model="rw2"))
# rw2 structure on the temporal component

vac.mnth.typeII.inla <- inla(vac.mnth.typeII , family="poisson",
                      data = vac.mnth, offset=log(population),
                      control.predictor =list(compute=TRUE),
                      control.compute = list(dic=TRUE), verbose=TRUE)


## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
vac.mnth.typeIII <- month_doses ~
  f(num_id, model="bym", graph=london.adj) +
  f(month, model="rw2") +
  f(month1, model="iid") +
  f(month.int,model="iid",
#iid on the temporal component
       group = num_id.int,
    control.group = list(model="besag", graph=london.adj))
# besag on the spatial component

vac.mnth.typeIII.inla <- inla(vac.mnth.typeIII , family="poisson",
                      data = vac.mnth, offset=log(population),
                      control.predictor =list(compute=TRUE),
                      control.compute = list(dic=TRUE))


## -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
vac.mnth.typeIV <- month_doses ~
  f(num_id, model="bym", graph=london.adj) +
  f(month, model="rw2") +
  f(month1, model="iid") +
  f(num_id.int, model="besag", graph=london.adj,
        #spatial component
    group=month.int, control.group = list(model="rw2"))
  #temporal component

vac.mnth.typeIV.inla <- inla(vac.mnth.typeIV , family="poisson",
                      data = vac.mnth, offset=log(population),
                      control.predictor =list(compute=TRUE),
                      control.compute = list(dic=TRUE))

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] vb.correction aborted warning
parts:
the output you attached is screeming for help...

the model needs to contact to simpler ones, otherwise this does not make
sense (to me, at least).

intrinsic priors needs to be scaled, otherwise, effect of priors depends
on the model.


for the poisson I would use

f(..., model="rw2", scale.model=TRUE,
hyper=list(prec=list(prior="pc.prec", param=c(0.5,0.01)))

and use 'bym2' instead of 'bym'.

use same prior for the iid model

use proper prior for the intercept
